name: Zelio E-Mobility Ltd
tagline: BSE-SME low-speed electric 2W and e-3W maker growing ~80% a year - genuine volume ramp, but already carrying a ~60x earnings multiple on a low-moat assembly business
business_overview: Zelio E-Mobility (BSE SME: 544563) manufactures, assembles and supplies electric two-wheelers under the Zelio brand - largely low-speed e-scooters that fall outside registration/licence requirements - and electric three-wheelers under the Tanga brand. It sold ~70,000 units in FY26 and is targeting >125,000 units in FY27.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 313.7 Cr, up ~82% YoY (from ~Rs 172 Cr); ~121% revenue CAGR over 4 years off a tiny base
PAT ~Rs 28.4 Cr (+75% YoY); EBITDA ~Rs 38 Cr, margin ~12.2%
fundamentals_narrative: The operating story is real: units and revenue have compounded at extreme rates off a small base, FY26 revenue grew ~82% and PAT ~75%, and the FY27 volume target (>125,000 units) implies another ~80% unit step-up. But two things hold it back for this screen. First, valuation - at ~60x earnings and ~5.7x sales the market has already priced in years of rapid growth, so a further 10x needs both sustained ~100%+ PAT growth AND multiple retention. Second, business quality - low-speed EV 2W assembly is a low-barrier segment: imported/assembled kits, thin ~12% EBITDA margins, intense competition from dozens of unlisted players, and a regulatory dependency (the low-speed licence exemption) that could change. EBITDA margin at ~12% shows scale is not yet delivering meaningful operating leverage.

value_chain.position: Downstream OEM/assembler - sources cells/motors/controllers, assembles and brands finished low-speed e-scooters and e-rickshaws
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Brand/distribution and battery cost; little component IP in-house
value_chain.note: 2W EV is on an S-curve (priority-2 theme), but the low-speed sub-segment is the most commoditised and regulation-sensitive part of it; margins accrue to whoever has brand + dealer network + battery scale, not to a small assembler adding capacity into a crowded field.

bull_case: Genuine, large volume ramp - ~70k units FY26 to a >125k FY27 target - in a structurally growing EV 2W/3W market (priority-2 theme)
Near-pure-play single-segment EV exposure, the reason @Aditya_joshi12 flagged it as an EV proxy
Consistent profitability while scaling (PAT +75% FY26), unlike several cash-burning EV peers
bear_case: ~60x earnings / ~5.7x sales already - the valuation prices in years of hyper-growth, leaving little margin of safety for a further 10x
Low-speed EV 2W assembly is a low-moat, low-margin (~12% EBITDA), intensely competitive segment with a regulatory dependency (licence-exemption for low-speed vehicles)
BSE-SME: thin liquidity, limited disclosure, no institutional or trusted-community coverage
Untrusted-X quiz mention only - a categorisation as an 'EV proxy', not a conviction call
verdict_headline: Real growth, wrong price - a low-moat low-speed-EV assembler already at ~60x earnings does not offer the risk/reward for a 10x/100x thesis
verdict_reasoning: External-lead (tier 4.5) from an untrusted X source (@Aditya_joshi12 teaching quiz, 2025-11-28) categorising it as a single-segment EV proxy - no conviction call, no floor

The small-cap live-inflection rule is meant for weak-history names that are cheap on a recent turn; Zelio is the opposite - the recent turn is already in the price at ~60x P/E, and the business (low-speed EV assembly, ~12% EBITDA, regulation-sensitive) has no moat to justify multiple retention through a 10x

Live-theme match: EV ecosystem, priority-2. Value-chain read: assembler 'adding' capacity at a low-pricing-power, commoditised node. thesis_fit neither, conviction Low. Revisit only on a large valuation reset or evidence of durable margin expansion

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: 'the business... has no moat to justify multiple retention through a 10x' (moat=no); low-speed EV is 'the most commoditised and regulation-sensitive part' of the EV S-curve (tailwind weak); 'the recent turn is already in the price at ~60x P/E' (valuation=no).
